interface.title: Colony Counter (colony·counter)
interface.stage_of_work: Measuring results: counting colonies (CFU) on incubated agar plates, then checking the count
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload a photo of an agar plate, get an automatic colony count drawn as rings on the photo, then click to add missed colonies, remove false ones and resize rings until the count can be trusted, and optionally save the corrected plate for training.

data.note: Uploaded agar-plate-colonies.jpg (two blood-agar plates held in gloved hands), agar-plate-staph.jpg (a figure with panels A–J showing staph plates and a micrograph, so not a real bench plate photo) and yeast-colonies-plate.jpg (a clear plate with many tiny specks). No gridded counting-plate photo was among the test files. No trained model is bundled, so /status returned {"model_available": false} and every detection ran on the classical computer-vision engine (header and count card say CLASSICAL CV).

features.name: Click-to-correct detection overlay with running tally
features.general: Draw automatic detections as markers on an image. The user clicks empty spots to add objects and clicks markers to remove them, while a panel keeps a live total split into auto / added / removed. A legend says where each kind of mark came from.
features.specific: Green rings for auto-detected colonies and amber rings for colonies you add; the legend also lists a dotted 'Recovered' style that never appeared on classical CV. Tap empty agar to add, tap a ring to remove. The Total Count card shows auto · added · removed.
steps: Look over the green auto rings on the plate photo
Tap a false ring (e.g. glove glare) to remove it; 'removed' goes up
Tap an unmarked colony to place an amber Added ring; 'added' goes up
Tap an amber ring again to take it away; 'added' goes down, 'removed' does not change
Read the Total Count
serves_tasks: Add objects the detector missed, and take back a mistaken addition
Read off the final count and how it was reached

features.name: Resizable markers by wheel or vertical drag
features.general: Change the size of a circular marker on an image by scrolling over it or by pressing and sliding up/down, so the marker matches the object's real size.
features.specific: Scroll on a ring, or press and slide up/down on it, to shrink or grow it to fit the colony. Each scroll changes the size only a little; dragging changes it a lot.
steps: Point at a ring
Scroll down to shrink it, or up to grow it
Or press on the ring and drag upward to enlarge it
serves_tasks: Change the size of a detection marker

features.name: Detection sensitivity that re-runs when released
features.general: A strict-to-lenient threshold slider that re-runs detection on the current image when released, so the user can try settings until the first pass looks right. The setting carries over to the next image. A split-touching-objects toggle sits beside it, but it acts only on a trained model's detections and does nothing with the fallback method.
features.specific: Sensitivity slider (low / standard / high) re-detects on release; it also responds to the End key. The 'Split merged colonies' checkbox needs the trained model; on CLASSICAL CV it left every count unchanged.
steps: Drag the Sensitivity slider (or press End on it) and let go
Watch the rings and the auto count update
Compare counts at low, standard and high and keep the setting that fits the plate
Only with the trained model: tick Split merged colonies to separate touching colonies
serves_tasks: Change the detector's sensitivity and re-run it
Turn on the step that splits touching objects

features.name: Reset and next-sample controls
features.general: Per-image session controls: throw away manual edits and re-detect from scratch, or move on to the next image while keeping the detection settings.
features.specific: Reset this plate clears edits and re-detects. Count another plate returns to the upload circle.
steps: Press Reset this plate to clear edits and get a fresh detection
Check that the card shows added 0 · removed 0
Press Count another plate to load the next photo
serves_tasks: Throw away manual edits and start over from a fresh detection
Move on to the next sample

features.name: Save corrected annotation to a training set
features.general: Human-in-the-loop data capture: after correcting an image, one button stores the corrected annotation for future model training and confirms with the number of objects saved.
features.specific: Save this plate for training changes to 'Saved N colonies ✓'. The README says this feeds the separate labeller/training loop; no dataset view is visible in the app.
steps: Correct the plate
Press Save this plate for training
See 'Saved N colonies ✓' match the Total Count

features.general: When automatic detection finds nothing, show a banner saying so and suggesting what to do: mark objects by hand or raise the sensitivity and re-run.
features.specific: Amber banner: 'Auto-detection found nothing to count here. Tap each colony to count it manually, or raise the sensitivity and re-run.'
steps: Upload a plate; detection returns 0
Read the banner
Raise the sensitivity or tap colonies by hand

features.name: Detection-engine indicator
features.general: Show the user which method produced the detections (trained model or fallback), so a reviewer knows how much to trust the first pass. A machine-readable status endpoint reports the same thing.
features.specific: Header badge and 'ENGINE: CLASSICAL CV' line on the count card; /status returns {"model_available": false}.
steps: Read the engine badge in the header
Read the ENGINE line on the Total Count card
Optionally open /status to confirm model_available
serves_tasks: Confirm whether the trained model or the fallback method is running
